The AEK-972 is a 5.56x45mm version of the AEK-971. It is compatible with the various magazines of the AK-100 rifle family such as the AK-101, AK-102 carbine and AK-108. Its purpose of being an export for Western Countries came short in The Zone, for some expensive black markets were able to acquire this variant and sell it around.

 %c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] Scopes for dovetail mount
 %c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] TGP-A suppressor
 %c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] GP-25 grenade launcher

The A-545 is a successor of the AEK-971 that saw limited service in the Russian Army, making it very rare even in The Zone. Other than its subtle improvements, which includes a more compact yet ergonomic sliding stock, a rotatory rear drum aperture sight and a two-round burst instead of three, the most obvious would be the lack of a dovetail mount in favour of a Picatinny rail, allowing it to use NATO scopes.
 %c[ui_gray_2]ATTACHMENTS:
 %c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] Scopes for Picatini rail
 %c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] TGP-A suppressor
 %c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] GP-25 grenade launcher

Based on previous AK rifles in internal design and layout, the AEK-971 is also equipped with a recoil-balancing mechanism, resulting in more controllable automatic fire. Small batches of this rifle were manufactured for the Russian MVD. This model specifically has a light-beige colour with red stains, symbolizing the Duty faction. Some mechanisms were reassembled or replaced with more reliable ones. Parts are fitted tighter which results in higher muzzle speed.

The AEK-973 is a 7.62x39mm version of AEK-971 developed at the Kovrov Mechanical Plant under the direction of Stanislav Ivanovich Koksharov based on SA-006 system. Based on previous AK rifles in internal design and layout, the AEK-973 is also equipped with a recoil-balancing mechanism, resulting in more controllable automatic fire. Small batches of this rifle were manufactured for the Russian MVD.
